basics.name: Yuheng Wang
basics.label: Ph.D. Student in Applied Physics
basics.summary: Applied Physics Ph.D. student at Rice University with undergraduate training in Engineering Physics, Computer Science, and Electrical and Computer Engineering. Interests: quantum physics, cavity QED, photonics, and AI/ML for scientific discovery.

work.name: University of Michigan, Department of Radiation Oncology
work.summary: Equating the biologically effective dose of SBRT and 90Y SIRT; ReMasker-Cox for survival-guided imputation.
highlights: Built a voxel-level pipeline aligning DGAE-MRI k1(x) maps to CT-based dosimetry with parenchyma masks and dose binning.
Harmonized modalities with LQ-based EQD2 for SBRT and protraction-aware BED for SIRT.
Modeled subvoxel SIRT nonuniformity via EUD and fit mixed-effects logistic dose-response with bootstrap uncertainty.
Extended ReMasker with a CoxPH loss and joint reconstruction-survival training for clinical tabular data.

work.name: University of Michigan, Deng Research Lab
work.summary: Loss-induced synthetic magnetic field; non-Hermitian exciton-polariton transport beyond Lorentz reciprocity theorem.
highlights: Designed and simulated rotationally asymmetric Si ring-resonator arrays to engineer loss-induced synthetic magnetic fields.
Built a non-Hermitian tight-binding model and validated phase/loss asymmetry remedies in simulation.
Used Ansys Lumerical to simulate a nanobeam cavity integrated with a grating coupler and prepared monolayer MoSe2 samples.
Manuscript submitted: Harnessing nanophotonic edgemodes by engineering PT symmetry.

projects.name: Coupled Flow Matching (CPFM): Controllable Dimensionality Reduction & Reconstruction
projects.summary: CPFM learns coupled continuous flows for data x and low-dimensional embeddings y to enable both p(y|x) sampling and p(x|y) reconstruction.
highlights: Extended Gromov-Wasserstein OT with a kernelized quadratic objective to encode semantic priors.
Derived an alternating minimization with entropic Sinkhorn and O(n^2) per-iteration complexity.
Implemented Dual Conditional Flow Matching with a shared drift network, role flagging, and mute-masking.
Evaluated on MNIST, CIFAR-10, TinyImageNet, AFHQ, and QM9 with semantically rich 2D embeddings and strong reconstructions.

projects.name: Analogical Analyses of Epidemic Evolution from the Fluid Mechanics View
